line1: What is due on your car

pieces.eyebrow: Two ways a job comes due

pieces.text: Whichever is further along its limit is the one that counts.

alt: A two-column card comparing how a car job comes due by miles and by months, with a note that whichever limit is reached first counts.
caption: Work out each job both ways: distance since it was done, and months since.

pieces.eyebrow: Before you hand over the keys

lines.label: Say
lines.text: An oil and filter change and a tire rotation, please.

lines.label: Then
lines.text: Please do not go over this without calling me first.

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: For anything else, please give me the estimate in writing.

items: Leave a number they can reach
Note the mileage and the date

alt: A three-line script for a repair shop: the specific job, a call before going over the limit, and a written estimate, plus optional extras.
caption: A plain script, not legal advice. Say the job, the limit and the call.

steps.what: Note what they recall, as theirs
The odometer number and today's date
It says how often each job comes round
Begin with today: date, miles, what was done

pieces.text: Treat each job as unknown until you have a real date for it.

alt: A four-step first-week timeline for a used car with no paperwork: ask the seller, note the mileage, find the manual, start a record.
caption: Four steps for the first week with a used car that came with nothing on paper.

pieces.text: Write what was done, not what you meant to do.

alt: A maintenance log table with columns for date, miles, what was done and who did it, marked as needed or optional, and a note to record facts.
caption: The columns of a simple log. Cost or note is a fifth, optional one.

pieces.text: Say what you can back up. Leave out what you cannot.

alt: A blank service record page with fields for date, miles, what was done, who did it and notes, beside a note to include only what you can back up.
caption: The shape of a record to print for a buyer. Keep receipts separately.

pieces.text: Towing, short trips, dust, heat or cold: check what the manual says for them.

alt: A blank three-row table with job, miles and months columns to fill in from the owner's manual, and a note about harder driving conditions.
caption: A page to copy your manual's intervals onto, once. Leave a column blank if the manual does.

pieces.text: Check the emergency kit is in the car and complete.

alt: A winter car checklist covering battery, tires, wiper blades, washer fluid and lights, with a note to check the emergency kit is complete.
caption: Five checks plus the emergency kit. Note the date, even if nothing needed doing.

pieces.title: Name or plate at the top

pieces.text: Look at both cars together, so you can see which one needs you.

alt: A blank one-page record for a single car with name or plate, job, miles, insurance and registration dates, and a note to review both cars monthly.
caption: Keep each car's record on its own page, and check both together.

alt: A comparison of what to keep in a glove box versus at home, beside a blank card with plate, VIN, oil, tire size, insurer and roadside number.
caption: Keep the details in the car and the originals at home.

pieces.caption: Act on any date that falls inside the next six weeks
pieces.foot: Write the next date down the day you renew

alt: A card showing six weeks as the look-ahead window for car paperwork dates, beside a checklist of the kind of paper, its date and where it is kept.
caption: Registration, insurance, inspection: note the paper, the date and where it is.

items: Start a record: date, miles, work
Put a card in the glove box

pieces.text: The date you got the car and its mileage that day is enough.

alt: A five-item first-week checklist for a new driver: manual, mileage, papers, a record and a glove box card, with a note on the first entry.
caption: None of it needs a garage: a notebook, a pen and about an hour.
